slides.title: Conversation messages
slides.subtitle: Start and continue a conversation, and retry without sending twice
slides.notes: Once a Session exists, the personal agent talks to the company in a conversation. This example starts one, continues it, and shows the one rule that makes retries safe: a message keeps its ID and its content.

slides.title: Why message IDs matter
slides.statement: A message ID is an **idempotency key**: the same ID always means the same message.
slides.notes: Networks fail in ambiguous ways: the request may or may not have arrived. PAP message IDs are user-global idempotency keys, so the host can send the exact same message again and the company handles it once.

slides.title: Who takes part

columns.heading: Agent tool
columns.content: Asks to start or continue a conversation. It never holds a credential.

columns.heading: Trusted host
columns.content: Generates message IDs, keeps each `Message`, and signs every request with DPoP.

columns.heading: Company agent
columns.content: Receives the messages and answers with the conversation's status and responder.

slides.notes: The agent tool asks; the trusted host does the work, generating IDs and holding the Session Token and DPoP proofs; the company agent answers. Authentication stays in DpopHttpClient and never enters the tool's inputs or results.

slides.title: Start, then continue

items.title: Generate
items.detail: A msg_ ID with at least 128 random bits

items.title: Continue
items.detail: A new message ID, 202 or a waited event page

slides.notes: The host generates a random message ID and posts the first message. The company answers 201 with the conversation ID, its status and who is responding. Every following message gets its own new ID; the company answers 202, or a page of events when the host asked to wait.

slides.title: Retrying after a network failure

rows.label: Reuse the ID, change the content
New ID for the same text

slides.notes: After an ambiguous failure, retry the very same Message object you kept. Reusing its ID with different content is refused with message_id_conflict. And a new ID would be a brand new message, so the company could act on it twice.

slides.title: What ConversationClient does
items: Bounds response bodies and rejects duplicate JSON members
Surfaces company error codes, never response bodies
slides.notes: Python and TypeScript both expose ConversationClient. It checks what comes back as strictly as what goes out, and reports the company's error codes without passing on response bodies. TypeScript also honours a caller's AbortSignal.

slides.title: What stays where
slides.notes: The model only learns the conversation's status. The token, the proofs, the pairwise user ID and the message IDs stay in the host.

slides.title: Run it yourself
slides.cta: The Pydantic AI example starts and continues one conversation against a local company
slides.notes: Reading the company's ordered events is its own example, conversation events. Streaming, handoff, Direct Conversations and closing each have theirs too.
